name: water
summary: Standing water, as MU paints it: an opaque sheet with the light already drawn on.
why: Roughness 0.08, by a distance the lowest here - steel's blade is 0.32. Water is the only
specular surface in Lorencia and getting it wrong in the rough direction is what makes a
Metallic 0.0 all the same. Water is a dielectric with a very strong specular response,
which is not the same thing as a metal, and the standard mistake is to reach for
Range 0.02, near nothing. Every other material here varies its roughness because real
surfaces are patchily worn; a body of water is uniformly water.
Depth 0.12 on a cast grain, which is the ripple. The sheet already draws its own
caustics as light and dark, so reading relief off that gives ripples that agree with the
highlights the artist painted - which is the one place this approach is not merely
What is missing is that it does not move. The client scrolls this sheet one repetition
every twenty seconds and displaces it with a wind term; that is a shader and the
material cannot hold it. Twelve percent of Lorencia is water, so it is worth doing.
